twoTracksPrinciple: Every pilot runs on two independent numbers, Resonance and Bleed. Neither ever produces a numeric combat bonus larger than +2 — the difference between a well-synced and poorly-synced pilot is what they're allowed to do, not how good they are at doing it.

resonance.status: NEEDS REWORK - not playable as written. Flagged by Ingram 2026-09-13: Resonance requires substantial work before it is functional, interesting or playable. The numbers below are the existing draft, retained so the rebuild has a starting point; they are NOT authoritative and nothing new should be built on top of them. See open-questions.json#resonance-playability and design/resonance-and-bleed.md.

bands.name: Absolute
bands.actionNote: Plus one free Strike/round ignoring the multiple attack penalty.

resonance.bandDesignNote: Sort each Frame's class abilities into these four bands at chargen. A Dead Weight Frame should still be competent — a big, dangerous, slow thing, not a joke. Duration is the pacing tool: once internal power runs out, the Frame is dead weight until reconnected. Ground crew's Umbilical Control role buys more of it.
resonance.actionEconomyRevisionNote: Nominal was 2 actions until 2026-09-06, and the design bible's line that 'most of the campaign is played at 2 actions' described that. Changed to 3, deliberately: SF2E is architecturally a three-action system — two-action activities consume a whole turn, its signature turn shapes need three, and the multiple attack penalty is built around a third attack being possible-but-unwise — so a 2-action baseline plays a degraded version of the system rather than a tense one. 3 actions is now the norm from Nominal upward. 2 actions is a PENALTY state with exactly two causes: Dead Weight sync (below 40%), and Frame damage (see frameEconomy / scale-and-chassis.md §8, where Degraded caps at 2 and Critical at 1 regardless of band). Analysis: design/resonance-and-bleed.md §2; the band spread across normal operating range drops from 3.3x to 2.2x as a result, while Dead Weight stays a genuine outlier at 5.7x below Absolute, which is correct for a failure state.
resonance.boundaryConvention: The design bible prints adjacent bands sharing a boundary digit (e.g. "40-65%" then "65-85%"). This file resolves that the standard way — bands are contiguous and non-overlapping (65% = Harmonised, not Nominal). Revisit if that's not the intent.

pushMechanic.description: A pilot may raise Resonance mid-scene by accepting Bleed.
pushMechanic.resolution: Resolve the push with a check using the kid's own stats (a Will save, a relevant skill) — this is the one place the level-1 sheet does direct, real work inside a level-12 scene.

bleed.status: NEEDS REWORK - not playable as written. Flagged by Ingram 2026-09-13 alongside Resonance. The existing investigation already found why: four inflows, one undefined outflow, one threshold across ten points, so points 1-9 do nothing. The numbers below are the existing draft, retained as a starting point; they are NOT authoritative. See open-questions.json#bleed-playability and design/resonance-and-bleed.md.
sources: Suppression (declining an Anchor-relevant conflict to protect deployability)

berserk.effect: Damage output roughly doubles; targeting stops discriminating between friend, foe, and terrain.
berserk.narrationRule: Do not narrate this from the cockpit — the player doesn't get to watch it happen to them.

bleed.visibilityMechanism: Resolved 2026-09-06. A pilot does not passively see their Bleed total, and it is not permanently hidden either — it is TESTED. Spending a discretionary slice on a harmonics/medical evaluation reveals the current value, and the same evaluation can also improve it (see timeEconomy.options#harmonics-evaluation). This makes tactical certainty a purchase in personal time, exactly the pattern contactPool.analysisDutyInteraction already establishes for the Contact Pool: 'tactical certainty is purchased with personal time — the same currency as everything else in this game.' It also fixes the real problem with hiding it outright, which is that Pushing is a trade and a trade with one side of the ledger concealed is a gamble rather than a decision (design/resonance-and-bleed.md §3).

anchors.gmLever: Anchors are the GM's primary lever on Resonance.

suppression.trigger: A player declines an Anchor-relevant conflict specifically to protect their deployability (plays their kid unrealistically conflict-avoidant to stay combat-ready).
suppression.designIntent: Closes the exploit where rational players make their kids blandly nice to everyone to keep the emotional game alive. Both doors cost something: having the fight costs capability, swallowing it costs stability.

frameEconomy.hpAsCampaignResource: Frame HP is a campaign resource, not an encounter resource. Frames do not heal between fights. They move down a damage-state track: Operational -> Degraded -> Critical -> Hulked.

repair.cost: Repairing a step costs technician-days, drawn from a single shared weekly pool the Directorate allocates.
repair.sharedPoolNote: Frame modification/customization draws from the exact same pool. Repairing a friend's Frame and upgrading your own compete directly for the same finite resource — this is the primary economic tension of downtime.

upgradePoints.confirmed: 2026-09-06. Frames DO level up (campaign-arc.md had already corrected the design bible on this; this adds the earning mechanism). Players earn upgrade points from downtime activities AND from winning both personnel- and Frame-scale combat, spend them on Frame upgrades, and enough points levels the Frame — a normal SF2E level-up carrying bespoke Frame feats and options.
upgradePoints.pool: INDIVIDUAL per pilot, not shared. Deliberately unlike technician-days: each pilot has their own repair crew (see repairCrew below), so investing in your own Frame never means taking from a squadmate.
upgradePoints.guaranteedFloor: Combat wins award points at both scales, so a Frame can never be stranded at level 12 by a player who spends their downtime elsewhere.
upgradePoints.levelDrift: Hard cap of ONE level either way from the pilot's own level. Rewards investment up to a point without letting Frame-focus become an overpowering strategy, and keeps encounter maths predictable. This supersedes campaign-arc.md's strict-lockstep line, which is annotated there.
upgradePoints.overInvestmentCost: No new mechanic needed — the existing systems already punish it. Upgrade work spends discretionary slices, so slices spent in the hangar are slices not spent resting: Exhaustion climbs, Bleed goes unmanaged for want of a Harmonics Evaluation slot, and untouched Anchors invite Suppression. All work and no rest punishes itself.

repairCrew.confirmed: 2026-09-06. Each pilot has their own repair crew — standing NPCs, not the PC-played Ground Roles — and the relationship carries real mechanical weight in both directions.
repairCrew.goodStanding: Treat them well and they go beyond the allocation. The user's own example: go out drinking with your repair crew and they might put in a night shift nobody asked them for.
repairCrew.neglected: A neglected crew provides less HP healing per repair.
repairCrew.whyItIsNotRedundantWithTechnicianDays: Two different axes. The technician-day pool is the Directorate's SHARED allocation — how much repair time you are granted, competed for between pilots. Crew standing is PERSONAL and scales how much you get OUT of that time. Allocation versus effectiveness.
repairCrew.terminologyWarning: Do not call these 'ground crew' in player-facing text. Ground Roles (campaign/ground-roles.json) are something else entirely — the PC-played roles the non-piloting kids take during a Contact.
repairCrew.namedChief: Confirmed 2026-09-09: each crew has one named head, six total (data/npcs/repair-chief-*.json, linked via npc.schema.json's crewChiefForRef). Currently placeholders — Ingram's own framing: 'six lesser NPCs who may grow into bigger more interesting roles later.'

floorAndBoost.principle: A crew is always working, whether or not the pilot shows up — 'repair crews are always working around the clock.' A guaranteed baseline HP repair happens automatically every technician-day cycle regardless of PC involvement (the floor). Direct PC involvement — showing up and working alongside the crew, not just spending the resource — restores substantially more HP than the floor alone, representing real labour, not a relationship-standing multiplier layered on top of it.

repairCrew.coversVehicles: Confirmed 2026-09-09, once chassis-catalogue.json existed to need it: a pilot's repair crew maintains their assigned vehicle (data/campaign/chassis-catalogue.json) as well as their Frame, drawing from the same technician-day allocation. Splitting a limited pool between Frame repair and vehicle repair is a real player choice, not two separate economies.

frameEconomy.deployability: Not all six Frames are necessarily deployable at once. A Degraded or Critical Frame may be riskier or unable to launch. When a Contact only calls for two or three Frames, the players choose the subset — the GM never has to force this; the repair economy does it for them.
frameEconomy.permanentLoss: A Frame that reaches Hulked can stay Hulked. Permanent loss of a personal Frame is on the table from the start (foreshadow it early, so when it happens it reads as the campaign keeping a promise, not GM cruelty). Confirmed 2026-09-09: this now applies equally to vehicles -- badly damaging or destroying a chassis in the Session Three drill/first-real-threat pairing is acceptable and expected, generating real repair backlog, same as a Frame. PC death is never the cost mechanism at either scale.

timeEconomy.slicesRevisionNote: Was 2, revised 2026-09-06 once the day gained a real four-quarter shape (morning/afternoon/evening/night) during UX design work — see design/ux-doctrine.md §3/§7a. One discretionary slice per quarter is now the intended granularity, not a smaller number spread across four.
timeEconomy.mandatoryLoad: School (morning + afternoon only) and sync training are standing options, on offer most days like anything else — choosing them still spends the quarter's slice, the same as any other pick. In practice they're the default most players take most days, which is what keeps a day feeling structured even though nothing forces the choice mechanically.
timeEconomy.designIntent: More options exist than slices to spend them on — that gap is the entire engine of downtime play.
timeEconomy.restIsAlwaysAvailable: Even a player with nothing else planned, or one running high on fatigue (see fatigue below), can always spend a quarter's slice resting instead. Encouraged, not just permitted.

options.name: Frame Modification
options.cost: 1+ slices, from the shared technician-day pool

options.name: Repair Advocacy
options.effect: Push a Frame back up the damage-state track.

options.name: Anchor Time
options.effect: Scene with an Anchor — a chance to affirm it (or risk it).

options.name: Analysis Duty
options.effect: Read the sensor archive: reveals the current Contact Pool state, or pushes the floor back (delays the next possible Contact).

options.name: Rest
options.effect: Recover — confirmed 2026-09-06 to be a category of several named rest activities, each with a different SF2E-relevant bonus (e.g. a quiet option weighted toward HP recovery, hospital care targeting HP and debuffs, a social outing for a different kind of bonus). The specific roster and numbers are not yet designed.

options.name: Harmonics Evaluation
options.effect: Get tested. Reveals the pilot's current Bleed value (otherwise not visible — see bleed.visibilityMechanism) and can also improve it. This is how a pilot buys the information needed to price a Push honestly: give up a morning, learn where you actually stand, and possibly come out of it better than you went in. Confirmed 2026-09-06; the amount of Bleed reduction it grants is not yet set.

fatigue.description: Working consecutive segments without resting triggers a check to see how tired the character is; the check gets harder each additional segment worked without a rest, and failing enough of them ends in involuntary unconsciousness and the loss of that segment's slot. Confirmed 2026-09-06 (design/ux-doctrine.md §3); grounded in but goes beyond PC2E's own flat "fatigued at 16 hours" rule (reference/srd/player-core/489-exploration-mode.json).
fatigue.resetBy: likely resting, exact mechanism not yet decided alongside the rest-activity-roster question

contactPool.activeFrom: Day 7 (the opening arc, Days 1-6, is hand-placed and does not roll).
contactPool.designIntent: Bounded on both ends by design: players are never punished with a zero-warning attack, and tension never gets an indefinite escape hatch either. Starting numbers below are a proposed baseline, not fixed — tune freely.

floor.description: No Contact can trigger within 2 quiet days of the last one. No roll happens during this window at all.

rollProcedure.description: Contact triggers on a 20. The target number drops by 1 for each additional quiet morning (20, then 19+, then 18+...) — visible, predictable, escalating.

ceiling.description: If Contact hasn't triggered by the 8th quiet morning (target would be 13+), it happens automatically. The pool can never coast forever.

contactPool.analysisDutyInteraction: Analysis Duty either reveals the current target number to the players, or spends a slice to push the floor back by a fixed number of days (a guaranteed delay). Either way, tactical certainty is purchased with personal time — the same currency as everything else in this game.

falseContact.sharedCost: All three types cost the same disrupted evening as a real Contact.

types.name: Genuine false positive
types.description: Full scramble, nothing there. Teaches players early that the cost of readiness isn't only the Claimants — the system itself has a price.

types.name: Role reversal
types.description: The scramble is real, but what needs help is people, not a fight. The Frames end up rescuing "children" (evacuees, civilians, possibly off-duty kids) rather than the other way around. Same adrenaline shape, subverted resolution.

types.name: First contact with the Watcher
types.description: A false or ambiguous response that is actually the first evidence of a second, invisible antagonist. Doesn't resolve as combat — resolves as an investigation hook, and shouldn't be closed out quickly.
